citations.assessment: The blessing baraita at the end of the daf explicitly names Ahavah son of Rabbi Zeira.
The baraita on divination explicitly names Ahavah son of Rabbi Zeira. The passage gives no location.
Rabbi Zeira directs his son Ahavah to teach the baraita on admitting new-moon testimony. The dispute over the disrupted song supplies the local context.
Rava uses the ornaments phrase as a rhetorical objection to relying on the named baraita. The following answer identifies a tannaitic dispute.
The homily on Lamentations 2:17 is indexed as Eikhah Rabbah 2:21 in this edition. It explicitly reads Ahavah son of Rabbi Ze’ira.
The saying about the ark reads Rav Achvah son of Rav Ze’ira. Preserve the digital titles as a witness detail.
The vineyard homily reads Achva son of Rabbi Ze’ira in the interpretation of the angels’ running. The edition indexes it at 8:10:2 despite its verse incipit.
The bread homily has Achvah bar Ze’ira. Another passage in the same chapter has Ahavah bar Ze’ira. Both occurrence forms are retained.
The homily attributes the concealed divine name interpretation to Achvah son of Rabbi Zeira. The following stories develop that interpretation.

The blessing-order argument indeed reads Achuyah in the name of Rabbi Ze’ira. Heilprin calls it a scribal error. The retrieved witness demonstrates the reading and leaves the proposed correction open.

Guggenheimer reads Achvah son of Rabbi Ze’ira in Rabbi Mana’s Caesarea report and supplies the bread analogy. Other indexed witnesses return a coordinate “and Rabbi Ze’ira” reading in discovery. Heilprin’s printed in-name-of reading and proposed son-of correction are both preserved.

The named occurrence is unlocated under this verse in the available digital witness. Retain the citation as printed. Retrieved and read Kohelet Rabbah 4:1:1, which has other attributed interpretations. Bounded searches for the incipit and Achvah/Achva variants did not locate a matching passage.

The exact errata clause remains uncollated. Acha bar Ze’ira remains a proposal attributed to Sedeh Yehoshua. Located the bibliographic listing of the Constantinople Zeraim edition (Halacha Brura library). Targeted phrase searches yielded Heilprin alone. The Bavli search returned Yaakov bar Acha reporting Zeira and other nearby words, without confirming the proposed patronym.

Keep the first-person nonfinding in its context of the proposed Bavli form. It cannot erase the Achvah readings in the midrashic and Yerushalmi witnesses. Compared the named Bavli units with the variants in Tanchuma, Bereshit Rabbah, Shir HaShirim Rabbah, Kohelet Rabbah, Challah and Pesachim.
